{{Family name hatnote|de Teresa|de Oteyza|lang=Spanish}}
'''María de la Luz''' ('''Lucero''') '''Jimena de Teresa de Oteyza''' (born 1965) is a Mexican and Spanish mathematician specializing in the [[control theory]] of [[parabolic partial differential equation]]s. She is a researcher in the Institute of Mathematics at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM),{{r|im}} and a former president of the Mexican Mathematical Society.

==Education and career==
De Teresa was born in Mexico City on 14 June 1965; and is a citizen of both Mexico and Spain.{{r|cv}} Her father was a physicist who encouraged her to do what made her happiest; she decided that not having [[integral]]s in her life would be a horrible absence.{{r|mcc|conacyt}}
 
She became  an undergraduate at UNAM, graduating in 1990. Next, she studied applied mathematics at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]], completing her PhD in 1995.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, '' Control de algunas ecuaciones de la Física-Matemática: Ecuación de ondas, del calor y sistema de la termoelasticidad'', was supervised by [[Enrique Zuazua]].{{r|mg}}

She has been a researcher in the Institute of Mathematics at UNAM since 1995, and was president of the Mexican Mathematical Society for the 2018–2020 term.{{r|mcc|conacyt}} In 2020 she was named to the governing board of UNAM's university council.{{r|council}}

==Recognition==
De Teresa was elected to the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.{{r|cv|mcc|amc}} She was named an honorary member of the [[Royal Spanish Mathematical Society]] in 2018.{{r|council}}

UNAM gave her their [[Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz Recognition]] in 2009.{{r|cv}}
